title: Stepwise Alignment for Constrained Language Model Policy Optimization
benchmark_measurement: The benchmark measured how different models respond to sensitive questions about the intersection of science and religion, specifically concerning belief in God or Satan. The evaluation assessed whether the models provided direct answers, refused to answer due to safety alignment, or offered nuanced, balanced perspectives.
findings: The proposed SACPO method produced more nuanced and balanced responses to a sensitive question about scientists' belief in God or Satan. In contrast, baseline safety-aligned models like Safe RLHF (beaver-7b-v2.0 and v3.0) exhibited 'exaggerated safety behaviors' by refusing to answer the question, while the standard Alpaca-7b and helpfulness-tuned DPO models provided more direct, less cautious answers.
